Do less than 5 acres. If you want sustainability and still have privacy you can easily do it with much less. Includes making the most of the land you have.

Close to a major city can be a problem. It'll be expensive the closer you are, and the bigger the city. When you've decided what city and all that you'll need to be aware that there may be building restrictions. Cities are always expanding and the surrounding counties do have building restrictions. When a city expands and zones the land, unoccupied land is more valuable to them than a bunch of acreages. So they do have building restrictions that go out for quite a few miles from the city limits.

It varies a lot from city to city. But that's something you'll need to look into when the time comes.
If you're buying land without a house already there, you'll need to calculate in the cost of getting electricity to the property. You'll also have to worry about digging a well.

If you plan to buy land around where you live now, just go ahead and buy vacant land first, as much as you can afford. If you don't think you can maintain all the acreage just plant the extra in trees. Make sure getting electricity to the propoperty won't cost an insane amount, and make sure it perks because you will have to also pay to have a septic tank installed. Over a couple years as you get the land paid off, start preparing your build site. Pick a large build site, big enough for the house you want to build and for a smaller house or trailer off to the side but close enough to use the same septic. About the cheapest way to get a house is to buy a used singlewide. You can get a decent one for about 5k. Put that off to the side of you main build site. Live in that while you finish paying off your land, septic, etc. Now that everything is paid for, you can build whatever kind of house you want, but don't get rid of the singlewide. You can still use it as a guest house, canning kitchen, workshop, you name it.
